key_insight: E-textile design is bottlenecked less by lack of ideas than by fragmented workflows and missing standardized, machine-readable representations that GenAI could help bridge.
engineering_relevance: For materials and wearable-systems teams, the paper points to AI tools that could accelerate cross-disciplinary e-textile design, prototyping, and manufacturing translation.
method: Two half-day co-design workshops were run in Shanghai and Winchester with practitioners from materials, electronics, garment design, HCI, and manufacturing.
Participants mapped their own e-textile design pipelines and annotated pain points and GenAI opportunities.
The authors synthesized proposed AI roles by pipeline stage and the conditions under which each would be useful.
evidence_signal: The evidence is qualitative workshop data from 20 Shanghai participants (10 with prior e-textile experience analyzed) plus 10 Winchester participants, using practitioner-generated process maps and annotations rather than quantitative benchmarking.
watch_item: Proposed GenAI support may be limited until e-textile designs can be represented in standardized, machine-readable forms.
paper_title: Mapping E-textiles Design Pain Points and Generative AI Opportunities: Insights from Workshops in Shanghai and Winchester
